unit-m5u1.title: Unit 5 · Lesson 1: Patterns for Dividing Multiples of 10
unit-m5u1.source: enVision Topic 5 Student Edition practice pages — dividing by two-digit divisors (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 5-1 practice pages: using basic facts and place-value patterns to divide multiples of 10, including missing dividends and divisors and word problems.

why.text: Every later lesson in this unit leans on this one. Estimating a quotient, and each step of the area model, divides by tens.

objectives.text: Divide multiples of 10 using a basic fact and place-value patterns
Find a missing dividend or divisor in a division with multiples of 10
Check a quotient by multiplying back
Put both amounts in the same unit before dividing

parentNote.text: Built from the lesson 5-1 practice pages in her Unit 5 folder, read for what they ask. The numbers are fresh, not the page's own. The trap most worth a word is the fact that borrows a zero: 4,000 ÷ 80 uses 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so the answer is 50, and counting that zero again gives 500. Two questions are built around it, and every wrong option comes from a named slip (a zero too many, a zero too few, the zeros of both numbers added on, or the borrowed zero counted twice). One question changes kilograms to grams first, like the page's own sea-salt problem.

nextUp.text: Fact first, then count the zeros, then multiply back to check.

cards.def:
**Cover the zeros and divide the digits that are left.**
• 2,700 ÷ 30 starts with 27 ÷ 3 = 9.
• Then the zeros finish the answer.

**490 ÷ 70 is the same as 49 tens ÷ 7 tens, which is 7.**
• Tens shared into groups of tens gives a plain number of groups.
cards.hint: 49 tens in groups of 7 tens: 7 groups.

cards.term: Count the zeros that are left
cards.def:
**Take away one zero for each zero in the divisor.**
• 28,000 ÷ 40: 28 ÷ 4 = 7, then three zeros minus one leaves two, so 700.

cards.term: When the fact needs a zero
cards.def:
**Sometimes the fact borrows a zero: 4,000 ÷ 80 uses 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so the answer is 50.**
• 8 does not divide 4, so the fact takes one zero from 4,000.
• That zero is used up. It does not get counted again.

**Taking one zero off the dividend AND the divisor keeps the answer the same.**
• 4,500 ÷ 50 = 450 ÷ 5 = 90.
cards.hint: Both numbers shrink together, so the answer stays put.

cards.def:
**Use multiplication to find a missing dividend or divisor.**
• ___ ÷ 80 = 600 means 600 × 80 = 48,000.
• 36,000 ÷ ___ = 900: 900 × 40 = 36,000, so the divisor is 40.

**Quotient × divisor should give back the dividend.**
• 700 × 40 = 28,000, so 28,000 ÷ 40 = 700 is right.
cards.hint: A wrong number of zeros shows up at once.

cards.def:
**Before you divide, put both amounts in the same unit.**
• 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams, so 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams.
cards.hint: Grams with grams, kilograms with kilograms.

questions.q: Why can you find 490 ÷ 70 by thinking "49 tens ÷ 7 tens"?
opts: Both numbers are counted in tens, and tens shared by tens gives ones
The zeros do not matter, so you can drop them from both numbers
70 has one zero, so the answer must always have one zero too
Every division by 70 has an answer of exactly 7
questions.hint: What is 490 written in tens? What is 70 written in tens?

ex.main: **Both are counted in tens.** 49 tens shared into groups of 7 tens is 7 groups, the same as 49 ÷ 7.
ex.tip: Taking the same zero off both numbers leaves the quotient alone.

steps: Zeros left to count: 2,700 has 2, 30 has 1, so 1 zero.

ex.main: **90.** Check: 90 × 30 = 2,700. The wrong answers come from real slips: 900 is one zero too many; 9 is one zero too few; 9,000 is the zeros of both numbers added on.
ex.tip: Each zero in the divisor cancels one zero in the dividend.

questions.q: Which basic fact helps you find 28,000 ÷ 40?
questions.hint: Cover the zeros. Which digits are left?

ex.main: **28 ÷ 4 = 7.** The fact uses the digits in front of the zeros, then the zeros finish the job: 700.
ex.tip: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 is a real fact, but it divides by the answer instead of by 4.

steps: Zeros left to count: 28,000 has 3, 40 has 1, so 2 zeros.

ex.main: **700.** Check: 700 × 40 = 28,000. The wrong answers come from real slips: 7,000 is one zero too many; 70 is one zero too few; 70,000 is the zeros of both numbers added on.
ex.tip: Check by multiplying back: your answer × 40 must give 28,000.

questions.hint: 8 does not divide 4. Which fact uses 40?
steps: 8 does not divide 4, so the fact borrows one zero: 40 ÷ 8.
Zeros left to count: 4,000 has 2 (after the borrowed one), 80 has 1, so 1 zero.

ex.main: **50.** Check: 50 × 80 = 4,000. The wrong answers come from real slips: 500 is the borrowed zero counted twice; 5 is one zero too few; 50,000 is the zeros of both numbers added on.
ex.tip: When the fact borrows a zero, that zero is used up.

steps: 4 does not divide 2, so the fact borrows one zero: 20 ÷ 4.
Zeros left to count: 20,000 has 3 (after the borrowed one), 40 has 1, so 2 zeros.

ex.main: **500.** Check: 500 × 40 = 20,000. The wrong answers come from real slips: 5,000 is the borrowed zero counted twice; 50 is one zero too few; 500,000 is the zeros of both numbers added on.

steps: 36,000 has three zeros and 900 has two.
One zero is left over for the divisor, so it is 40.

ex.main: **40.** 900 × 40 = 36,000. With 4 the quotient is 9,000, with 400 it is 90, and with 4,000 it is 9.
ex.tip: Multiply your answer by 900 to check it lands on 36,000.

questions.hint: The missing number is the dividend. Multiply to find it.
steps: 600 has two zeros and 80 has one: three zeros in all.

ex.main: **48,000.** 600 × 80 = 48,000. 4,800 has a zero too few (4,800 ÷ 80 = 60), and 680 adds 600 and 80 instead of multiplying.
ex.tip: Undo a division with a multiplication.

questions.q: A sticker shop packs 5,400 stickers into rolls of 60. How many rolls does it fill?
opts: 90 rolls
900 rolls
9 rolls
9,000 rolls
steps: Zeros left to count: 5,400 has 2, 60 has 1, so 1 zero.

ex.main: **90 rolls.** Check: 90 × 60 = 5,400. The wrong answers come from real slips: 900 rolls is one zero too many; 9 rolls is one zero too few; 9,000 rolls is the zeros of both numbers added on.

questions.q: A theater sold 35,000 tickets over 70 shows, the same number for every show. How many tickets did it sell for each show?
opts: 5,000 tickets
500 tickets
50 tickets
50,000 tickets
steps: Zeros left to count: 35,000 has 3, 70 has 1, so 2 zeros.

ex.main: **500 tickets.** Check: 500 × 70 = 35,000. The wrong answers come from real slips: 5,000 tickets is one zero too many; 50 tickets is one zero too few; 50,000 tickets is the zeros of both numbers added on.
ex.tip: Each show sold the same number, so this is a sharing division.

questions.q: Which division has a quotient of 90?
questions.hint: Work out each one with the fact 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and count the zeros.
steps: 3,600 ÷ 40: two zeros minus one leaves one, so 90.
360 ÷ 40: one minus one leaves none, so 9.
3,600 ÷ 400: two minus two leaves none, so 9.

ex.main: **3,600 ÷ 40.** It is the only one that leaves exactly one zero after the fact 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Check: 90 × 40 = 3,600.
ex.tip: Same fact, different zeros, different answers. Count them every time.

questions.q: Which division has the same quotient as 4,500 ÷ 50?
questions.hint: What happens if you take one zero off BOTH numbers?
steps: 450 ÷ 5 takes one zero off each number: 450 ÷ 5 = 90.

ex.main: **450 ÷ 5.** Taking one zero off the dividend AND the divisor leaves the quotient the same: both are 90.
ex.tip: Taking a zero off only one of the numbers changes the answer by ten times.

questions.q: A cook uses 40 grams of pepper in each pot of soup. Pepper comes in a 2-kilogram jar or a 500-gram jar. Which jar gets used up exactly, with no pepper left over? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams.)
opts: The 2-kilogram jar, because 2,000 ÷ 40 = 50 with nothing left
The 500-gram jar, because 500 ÷ 40 = 12 with nothing left
The 2-kilogram jar, because 2 ÷ 40 comes out to a whole number
Both jars, because 40 divides any number that ends in zero
questions.hint: Change kilograms to grams first, so both jars use the same unit.
steps: So the 2-kilogram jar is used up exactly.

ex.main: **The 2-kilogram jar.** 2,000 grams makes exactly 50 pots. The 500-gram jar makes 12 pots and leaves 20 grams.
ex.tip: Both amounts have to be in grams before you can compare them.

questions.q: Ben says 8,000 ÷ 20 = 4,000, because 8 ÷ 2 = 4 and 8,000 has three zeros. What went wrong?
opts: He used the wrong fact, because 8 ÷ 2 is 6
The zero in 20 cancels one of them, so it is 400
Nothing went wrong, because 4,000 is correct
He should add the zeros, so the answer is 40,000
steps: 8,000 has three zeros, but 20 has one, and it cancels one of them.

ex.main: **The zero in 20 cancels one zero.** 8,000 ÷ 20 = 400, and 400 × 20 = 8,000.
ex.tip: Multiplying back catches a wrong number of zeros right away.
